_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Peoples and Forest Settlement
910.label: Event
910.description: BaKa and other Pygmy hunter-gatherers inhabit the equatorial rainforest; early Bantu-speaking farmers arrive bringing iron smelting and agriculture.

910.name: BaKa and Pygmy Forest Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: Indigenous hunter-gatherer communities in Gabon's dense equatorial rainforest; among the earliest inhabitants of the region.

910.name: Early Bantu Settlement and Ironworking
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking farmers migrate into Gabon; ironworking sites in the Ogooué River valley; gradual forest clearance for agriculture.

910.name: Okanda and Ancient Iron Sites
910.label: Event
910.description: Ancient iron-smelting sites in the Lopé-Okanda region represent some of the earliest metallurgy in Central Africa; UNESCO World Heritage landscapes.

910.name: Lopé-Okanda Iron Age Sites
910.label: Event
910.description: Extensive iron-smelting remains in the Lopé National Park area; rock engravings; evidence of early forest-savanna boundary management by human communities.

920.name: Fang Migration into Gabon
920.label: Event
920.description: The Fang people migrate southward from Cameroon and become Gabon's largest ethnic group; warrior culture, Bieri ancestor worship, and forest adaptation.

920.name: Fang Southward Movement
920.label: Event
920.description: Fang clans push through the equatorial forest; absorb or displace earlier Bantu groups; establish villages along river corridors; segmentary lineage system.

920.name: Fang Art and Bieri Tradition
920.label: Event
920.description: Fang create renowned Bieri reliquary figures; elaborate initiation ceremonies; rich oral traditions; artistic heritage later prized by European modernists.

920.name: Mpongwe and Orungu Coastal Trading States
920.label: Event
920.description: Mpongwe and Orungu peoples dominate the Gabon Estuary and Ogooué Delta; middlemen in slave, ivory, and dyewood trade with Europeans.

920.name: Mpongwe Trade at the Gabon Estuary
920.label: Event
920.description: Mpongwe clans control trade at the Gabon Estuary (Libreville area); intermediaries between European ships and interior peoples; accumulate wealth and adopt some European customs.

920.name: Orungu Kingdom of the Ogooué Delta
920.label: Event
920.description: Orungu kings dominate the Ogooué River delta and Cape Lopez; major slave-exporting polity; negotiate with Dutch, French, and British traders.

930.name: Slave Trade and French Establishment
930.label: Event
930.description: Portuguese reach the Gabon Estuary 1472; slave and ivory trade dominated by European companies; France establishes control through treaties with Mpongwe chiefs.

930.name: Portuguese Contact and Early Trade
930.label: Event
930.description: Portuguese traders name the Gabon estuary (from 'gabão', a hooded cloak); trade in slaves, ivory, and redwood with coastal peoples.

930.name: French Treaties and Founding of Libreville
930.label: Event
930.description: Captain Bouët-Willaumez signs treaties with Mpongwe chiefs 1839; French naval base established; freed slaves settle at Libreville ('Free Town') 1849.

940.name: French Colonial Gabon (1880–1960)
940.label: Event
940.description: Gabon becomes part of French Equatorial Africa; Brazza explores the Ogooué; concessionary companies, timber exploitation, and Albert Schweitzer's hospital.

940.name: Brazza's Ogooué Expeditions
940.label: Event
940.description: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza ascends the Ogooué River; establishes French claims in the interior; treaties with Fang and other chiefs.

940.name: Concessionary Companies and Timber
940.label: Event
940.description: Concessionary companies exploit rubber and ivory; after 1920 timber (okoumé) becomes principal export; forced labour for logging and porterage.

950.name: Independence and Léon Mba
950.label: Event
950.description: Léon Mba leads Gabon to independence; one-party rule; 1964 coup attempt reversed by French military intervention; Mba grooms Omar Bongo.

950.name: Gabon Independence
950.label: Event
950.description: Gabon independent 17 August 1960 under Léon Mba; BDG single-party rule; close ties with France; manganese and uranium mining begins.

950.name: 1964 Coup and French Intervention
950.label: Event
950.description: Military coup briefly deposes Mba; French paratroopers restore him within 24 hours under defence agreements; first French military intervention in post-colonial Africa.

950.name: Omar Bongo Dynasty (1967–2009)
950.label: Event
950.description: Omar Bongo (later El Hadj Omar Bongo Ondimba) rules for 42 years; oil wealth funds patronage; master of Françafrique diplomacy; multiparty reforms.

950.name: Omar Bongo's Rise and Oil Boom
950.label: Event
950.description: Albert-Bernard Bongo becomes president at 31; oil production booms from 1970s; single-party PDG state; converts to Islam 1973; renames to El Hadj Omar Bongo.

950.name: Multiparty Transition and Continued Rule
950.label: Event
950.description: Prodemocracy protests and Port-Gentil riots 1990; national conference; multiparty elections but Bongo wins each time; dies in office June 2009 after 42 years.

960.name: Ali Bongo Ondimba and the 2023 Coup
960.label: Event
960.description: Ali Bongo succeeds his father; disputed elections; stroke 2018; military coup August 2023 ends the Bongo dynasty after 56 years.

960.name: Ali Bongo Presidency
960.label: Event
960.description: Ali Bongo wins contested election 2009 (Port-Gentil riots); re-elected 2016 amid violent post-election crisis; suffers stroke 2018; questions about fitness to govern.

960.name: 2023 Military Coup
960.label: Event
960.description: Military officers led by General Brice Oligui Nguema overthrow Ali Bongo minutes after disputed election results announced August 2023; ends 56-year Bongo dynasty; transition government.
